source.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Chung-Pa Lee; Jihoon Kwon; Kyle Min; Jy-yong Sohn

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure/table formatting are flattened, but the document is usable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes and experimentally measures how sparse-autoencoder feature directions are represented and shared, using a different setup from the original toy-model study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on feature-direction mismatch, capacity-limited sharing, synthetic feature collapse, and SAE feature coherence in VLM embeddings. Retrieval and classification scores are omitted because they evaluate the proposed method’s downstream performance rather than the claim’s representational object. Figure-only values are recorded as such.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes the linear representation hypothesis and uses SAEs as a tool on VLM joint embeddings. Its results concern how SAE dictionaries assign cross-modal feature directions to decoder columns, plus the performance of its own modality-specific SAE method. It never measures whether a trained network stores more features than dimensions, nor where neuron polysemanticity comes from. Theorem 1's 'limited capacity' (m < 2n) is SAE dictionary width, not network superposition. The synthetic data (2048 features in d = 256) are superposed by construction, not learned. No row measures what any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim that cross-modal feature heterogeneity drives modality split in shared SAEs, and that auxiliary alignment losses trade reconstruction for latent alignment (Propositions 1–2). They report that modality-specific SAEs with post-hoc Hungarian alignment improve retrieval and steering without losing reconstruction.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops theory and experiments for cross-modal SAE feature directions and alignment, rather than reproducing the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical sharing result depends on whether latent capacity is above or below 2n. Synthetic feature collapse and reconstruction depend on the distance between corresponding cross-modal directions. The real-model direction analysis is reported for base- and large-size VLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: In eight CLIP-family VLMs, SAE decoder directions for strongly coactivating image and text latents are not aligned. Distance distributions stay above zero even at c ≥ 0.8. Examples: baseball, dcos 0.42; policeman, dcos 0.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLM joint embeddings, the same concept can be encoded by different feature directions across modalities (cross-modal feature heterogeneity).

fits_no_version.finding: Theory and synthetic experiments show that a reconstruction-only SAE assigns distinct directions to separate latents when wide enough. When narrower than the number of features, it merges geometrically close directions into one column at a reconstruction cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latent assignment depends on dictionary width and direction geometry, so modality split arises from directional mismatch.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea (2026)
record.problems: The authors state that the analysis relies on the linear representation hypothesis and simplified generative assumptions. Coactivation correlation is used as a proxy for semantic correspondence. The reported real-model direction distributions and monosemanticity curves are figure-only in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Table 1 and Appendix E.2 retrieval, classification, reconstruction, and other downstream task scores because they evaluate the proposed alignment method rather than the claim’s feature geometry or capacity mechanism. Omitted Figure 6 alignment-loss comparisons for the same reason.

untested.parts: All of it: no network is trained to compress sparse features, and there is no geometry, phase transition or orthogonality measurement.
All of it: no neurons are examined, and capacity results concern SAE dictionary width only.
All of it: VLM embeddings only, and no test of spread across neurons or of SAE recovery in LLMs.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features are not tested. Theorem 1 implies SAE latents depend on dictionary width, but only as theory under assumed data.
All of it: features are assumed to be one-dimensional directions.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R1–R8 to V1 and V2 because of the word 'capacity'. That capacity is SAE dictionary width, not network dimension, and the superposed synthetic features are imposed by the data generator. The paper assumes superposition and linear representations rather than testing them. It cites Toy Models only as background.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish nearly orthogonal feature geometry, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric arrangements; its theoretical capacity result concerns SAE decoder columns and the limit s→1.

The paper analyzes feature sharing among SAE decoder columns, not polysemantic neurons in the underlying VLM. It does not independently test a general rule that important features receive dedicated neuron dimensions.
No alternative, non-capacity mechanism for polysemantic neurons is tested.
The real-model experiments use VLM embeddings, not LLM activations; the paper does not test feature spread across LLM neurons.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. Cross-modal direction mismatch alone does not establish those properties.
The paper models features as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: joint SAE (theoretical)
rows.stage_stated: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the reconstruction-loss minimizer as sparsity parameter s approaches 1

conditions.value: at least 2n coordinates for 2n image and text feature directions

rows.measure: Reconstruction loss and assignment of feature directions to decoder columns
rows.value: The leading-order minimizer assigns a separate decoder column to each feature direction; total reconstruction loss is o(1−s).
rows.note: Analytical result for the paper’s SAE model, not an experiment on VLM neurons.
rows.check: Corollary 1 is an analytical result about SAE decoder columns when SAE width m ≥ 2n. It says nothing about a network storing sparse features as nearly orthogonal directions (V1) or about neurons competing for capacity (V2).

rows.subject: joint SAE (theoretical)
rows.stage_stated: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Characterize the reconstruction-loss minimizer under limited latent capacity

conditions.value: fewer coordinates than the 2n image and text feature directions

rows.measure: Feature assignment to decoder columns and reconstruction loss
rows.value: Directions are partitioned among m columns; each column is a top eigenvector of the sum of the assigned directions’ weighted outer products. The reconstruction loss is greater than zero for s sufficiently close to 1.
rows.note: The partition weights directions by E[zi² | zi ≠ 0]; the result describes shared SAE directions and residual reconstruction error.
rows.check: Theorem 1 describes SAE latents merging distinct directions when dictionary width is below the feature count. That is a dictionary-capacity result, not network superposition or neuron polysemanticity, and it is derived under assumed generative data rather than measured.

rows.subject: shared SAE (synthetic embeddings)
rows.stage_stated: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measure cross-modal feature collapse rate while varying distance between corresponding feature directions

conditions.value: dcos varied; text describes close but non-identical directions

rows.measure: Fraction of same-concept image/text feature pairs assigned to the same latent coordinate
rows.note: The text says the shared SAE collapses directions when they are geometrically close but not identical.
rows.check: The collapse rate is for a shared SAE on synthetic embeddings whose superposition is built into the data generator. It measures SAE latent assignment, not a learned network's feature storage.

rows.subject: modality-specific SAEs (synthetic embeddings)
rows.size_stated: m = 4096 per modality; embedding dimension d = 256
rows.stage_stated: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measure cross-modal feature collapse rate while varying distance between corresponding feature directions
rows.measure: Fraction of same-concept image/text feature pairs assigned to the same latent coordinate
rows.note: The text says modality-specific SAEs avoid collapse; the comparison matches total trainable parameters.
rows.check: This comparator is the study's own design choice. Separate image and text SAEs cannot assign image and text features to a shared column by construction, so 'absent' collapse is trivial.

rows.stage_stated: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measure embedding reconstruction while varying distance between corresponding feature directions
rows.measure: Reconstruction error
rows.note: The text reports higher reconstruction error for the shared SAE when distinct corresponding directions are represented by one decoder column.
rows.check: This is the reconstruction error of a shared versus modality-specific SAE design. It is a comparison of methods, not a superposition measure. The value is figure-only.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Theoretical SAE analysis with sparse features and latent capacity below the number of image and text feature directions; synthetic shared-SAE experiments
reader_labels.reason: Limited capacity leads to directions sharing decoder columns and to feature collapse for close but distinct directions (R2, R3). The paper does not test the claimed near-orthogonal geometry or a sparsity transition.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Theoretical SAE representation and synthetic shared-SAE setting
reader_labels.reason: When latent capacity is limited, distinct feature directions are grouped onto shared decoder columns; the grouping depends on weighted feature-direction matrices (R2, R3). This is SAE-level evidence, not a direct test of polysemantic neurons.
